disease_label_per_paper: Cryopyrinopathy / Muckle-Wells syndrome overlap in an Indian family associated with NLRP3 p.D303N
presentation_summary: 27-year-old Indian male proband admitted with recurrent high-grade intermittent fever, occipital headache, conjunctival congestion, and rash for 17 years.
Rash was migratory, non-pruritic, maculopapular, mainly over chest, abdomen, and extensor limbs, and worsened with cold exposure.
He had 3-4 episodes per month, each lasting 2-3 days, plus 17 years of asymmetric non-deforming polyarthritis involving axial and appendicular joints.
He had slowly progressive hearing loss for 10 years and exam showed short stature, short neck, conjunctival congestion, diffuse urticarial rash, clubbing, and bilateral papilledema.

Labs showed extreme leukocytosis, elevated CRP, normal renal/liver/urinalysis, negative RF/ANA/ANCA, severe bilateral sensorineural hearing loss, CSF lymphocytic pleocytosis with high protein, negative CSF microbiology, and neutrophilic perivascular skin inflammation.
NLRP3 p.D303N mutation, paper diagnosis, and inability to access IL-1 therapy are preserved as confirmatory or treatment context.
